title: no_std, embedded systems, and resource budgets

questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “no_std, embedded systems, and resource budgets”?
options: A no_std program needs a panic handler and platform-specific startup/linker setup.
Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects.
Rust bindings are immutable unless declared mut.
Obtain the installer from rust-lang.org and install native prerequisites only for the target you need.
questions.answer: A no_std program needs a panic handler and platform-specific startup/linker setup.
questions.explanation:
A no_std program needs a panic handler and platform-specific startup/linker setup.
Why: Rust can use `no_std` for firmware that cannot rely on OS services from the standard library, while `core` and platform abstractions such as embedded-hal remain available. Measure heap, stack, flash, RAM, and interrupt latency for the actual chip and linker configuration. `no_std` alone guarantees neither real-time behavior nor hardware safety; review HALs, drivers, and unsafe boundaries.
